questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning of Governance' refers to.
questions.a: Governance is the process by which a group, society, or country is directed, controlled, and managed to ensure order and welfare.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning of Governance'.
questions.a: Governance involves making decisions, implementing rules, and providing services so that society functions smoothly and fairly.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning of Governance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Understanding Governance

concepts.title: Levels of Government: Local, State, and National

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Levels of Government: Local, State, and National' refers to.
questions.a: Government in India functions at three levels: local (village, town, city), state, and national, each handling matters within its area.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Levels of Government: Local, State, and National'.
questions.a: Local government handles nearby issues, state government manages state-wide matters, and the national government deals with the whole country.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Levels of Government: Local, State, and National' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Levels of Government

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Democratic Governance' refers to.
questions.a: Democratic governance is a system in which people choose their representatives through elections and the government acts according to the will of the people.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Democratic Governance'.
questions.a: In a democracy, power lies with the people, who elect representatives to make decisions and govern on their behalf.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Democratic Governance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Democracy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Participation in Governance' refers to.
questions.a: Participation in governance means citizens take part in decision-making, elections, public meetings, and community activities that shape how they are governed.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Participation in Governance'.
questions.a: When citizens vote, attend gram sabhas, give feedback, or join campaigns, they actively contribute to how their society is governed.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Participation in Governance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Citizen Participation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Elections and Voting' refers to.
questions.a: Elections are the process by which people choose their representatives by voting, and voting is the act of expressing one's choice for a candidate.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Elections and Voting'.
questions.a: Through elections and voting, citizens select leaders who will make decisions and govern on their behalf in a democracy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Elections and Voting' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Elections

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role of Citizens in Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: Citizens in a democracy play an active role by voting, paying taxes, following laws, and holding representatives accountable for their actions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role of Citizens in Democracy'.
questions.a: A democracy works well when citizens are informed, participate in governance, and fulfil their duties towards society.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role of Citizens in Democracy' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Citizens in Democracy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Rights and Responsibilities of Citizens' refers to.
questions.a: Rights are freedoms and entitlements guaranteed to citizens, while responsibilities are duties citizens must perform to support society and democracy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rights and Responsibilities of Citizens'.
questions.a: Citizens enjoy rights such as education and equality, and in turn hold responsibilities like obeying laws and respecting others' rights.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rights and Responsibilities of Citizens' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Rights and Responsibilities

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Importance of Democratic Governance' refers to.
questions.a: Democratic governance is important because it gives people a voice, ensures equality, protects freedoms, and makes the government accountable to citizens.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Importance of Democratic Governance'.
questions.a: Democracy allows every citizen to participate, treats people equally, and ensures that leaders answer to the people who elected them.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Importance of Democratic Governance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Importance of Democracy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Grassroots Democracy and Local Self-Government' refers to.
questions.a: Grassroots democracy means giving people power at the local level through institutions like gram panchayats and municipalities to manage their own affairs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Grassroots Democracy and Local Self-Government'.
questions.a: Local self-government bodies, such as panchayats in villages and municipalities in towns, allow citizens to govern matters close to their daily lives.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Grassroots Democracy and Local Self-Government' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Grassroots Democracy
